progress_records.content: GOAL: Start review of five proposals against scope contract and frozen evidence bundles. READ: the five proposal texts and their five evidence bundles (d69fbb2eeb4c9ab0 cohrank-curvature-sinkhorn-v1, 6b5ae2abeecaab25 CURV_COH_PREFIX_SINKHORN, df96b282930cef5f curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1, bc49cd02b60c2754 hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1, 73aab3babfa88c58 scc-l1-curvcoherence). OBSERVED: all five share the identical sanity-check block: E11 PASS geometry_operator_valid, E12 FAIL behavior_dependency (a positive row scalar cannot move an arg-min), E13 PASS geometry_dependency (matched Euclidean intervention changed 1 top-1 index), E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN. Also E5/E6 identical train-only stats (118315 edges, mean out deg 5.45; baseline SID same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067) and identical Stage-3 ledger (best observed 0.0546 BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL, none at/above 0.065). REASONING: every bundle reports the generic behaviour-dependency proxy as FAIL, so differentiation must come from whether the proposal's own cost offset is codeword-dependent (can move the balanced plan) and from whether the design keeps the baseline's balanced assignment. Open: item-by-item scope compliance and ranking.

GOAL: Decide item-by-item scope compliance and ranking grounded in the bundles. READ: the five SPECIFICATION blocks and each bundle's E6/E11-E14 ledger lines. OBSERVED: (a) all bundles share E12 FAIL behavior_dependency (a positive row scalar cannot move an arg-min; only a codeword-dependent offset moved top-1 indices) so the only admissible behaviour injection is a CODE-INDEXED offset inside the balanced cost; (b) E13 PASS geometry_dependency (matched Euclidean control changed 1 top-1 index); (c) E14 CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN in all five, so joint reach is unproven for every candidate; (d) E6 baseline same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067, i.e. the baseline prefix carries only a weak behaviour signal, so a level-1-only intervention is the proportionate (and lowest-risk) bet; (e) ledger: every behaviour/curvature-ish arm sits below 0.065 (BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL 0.0546, CURV-RESID-CONTRAST 0.0544, CONCMID-GEO-SID 0.0517, COOC_RANK_FRECHET 0.0500, BEHDIR-L4 0.0482, BRad-RQ 0.0306/0.0446), all marked comparable_to_frozen:false. REASONING: rank by (i) does the offset depend on the codeword (E12) and stay inside a verbatim Sinkhorn with the baseline hard rule, (ii) derived-not-tuned constants, (iii) minimality of added machinery. Result: 1 curvature-stratum-sinkhorn-v1 (only the level-1 cost matrix changes, no extra loss, quantile-init strata, beta=measured median, levels 2-3 untouched); 2 CURV_COH_PREFIX_SINKHORN (code-indexed a_k, median/stop-grad-derived weights, level-1 only); 3 cohrank-curvature-sinkhorn-v1 (derived medians but offset applied to all three levels; own hypothesis concedes balancing may erase it); 4 hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1 (arbitrary-sign centred radius rhat_k, minibatch-induced-edge contrastive likely near-empty); 5 scc-l1-curvcoherence (self-admitted risk the capped offset is inert, double Sinkhorn, batch-median normalisation perturbs the baseline's effective entropy strength, circular buffered b_k). All five are in scope on switches/ablation-free design; none needs a sweep or a seed repeat. Open: none. ANSWER BLOCK follows in the next record.

t loss that flattens toward a bimodal encoding (its own risk list) and a per-batch median lambda_b. hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1 normalises d_c by D_med yet sets lambda=1 on a [-1,1]x(-1,1) product so the offset is commensurate with the whole distance term, uses an unnormalised homophily weight lambda=1 beside reconstruction, and leaves rhat_k sign arbitrary (E12/E13 say that is where it breaks). scc-l1-curvcoherence is last: two Sinkhorn passes plus detached running b_k buffers, a hard-coded 0.25 offset weight in the spec that its own risk line describes as a derived half-median cap (constant provenance defect under policy), and a W=5 window that departs from the baseline graph; its own risk list names inertness.

OBSERVED: (a) all five keep Sinkhorn and take the hard index as row-argmax of the balanced plan (criterion 6 satisfied, none out of scope); (b) all five inject a codeword-dependent, not row-scalar, behaviour offset (m_k via sigmoid, s_k=sigmoid(a_k) quantiles, a_k=tanh(sqrt(c)||e_k||), rhat_k centred radius, b_k from a first Sinkhorn plan), so none is trivially inert per E12 — but E12 sets the bar: a per-code offset must be large enough to reorder top-1, and E13 shows the curved-vs-Euclidean difference itself moves only 1 of 6 indices, so a small normalised offset will not act; (c) E5 shows a sparse graph (mean out-degree 5.45), so triangle-closure t_ij is near-zero for most pairs and every triangle-based rho/kappa/s_i is weak and popularity-adjacent — this penalises mechanisms that apply the offset broadly or add an unnormalised second loss, and rewards level-1-only, scale-relative, single-offset designs; (d) E6 shows the baseline L1 prefix already sits 0.0907 vs 0.067 null, so the coarse level is exactly where the small behaviour signal lives; (e) ledger E18–E25: best recorded Stage3 test R@10 is 0.0546 (BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL), then 0.0544 (CURV-RESID-CONTRAST), 0.0517 (CONCMID-GEO-SID), 0.0500 (COOC_RANK_FRECHET), 0.0482 (BEHDIR-L4), 0.0446 and 0.0306 (BRad-RQ); all comparable_to_frozen=false, none near 0.065.

CURV_COH_PREFIX_SINKHORN is close behind (lambda_b and lambda_curv scale-derived by stop-gradient, behaviour offset level-1 only, geometry at all levels) but carries a second alignmen

t loss that flattens toward a bimodal encoding (its own risk list) and a per-batch median lambda_b. hyperbolic_behavior_curvature_sinkhorn_v1 normalises d_c by D_med yet sets lambda=1 on a [-1,1]x(-1,1) product so the offset is commensurate with the whole distance term, uses an unnormalised homophily weight lambda=1 beside reconstruction, and leaves rhat_k sign arbitrary (E12/E13 say that is where it breaks). scc-l1-curvcoherence is last: two Sinkhorn passes plus detached running b_k buffers, a hard-coded 0.25 offset weight in the spec that its own risk line describes as a derived half-median cap (constant provenance defect under policy), and a W=5 window that departs from the baseline graph; its own risk list names inertness.
